transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I just feel worn out all the time. It's like... even if I get a full night's sleep, I wake up and my body feels like it's made of sandbags. Just getting through my workday or doing something simple like folding laundry takes absolutely everything I have.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Yeah, I have. Most days, honestly. I just wake up with this... heavy, flat feeling right in my chest. Sometimes I'll just sit at the kitchen table with my coffee, staring out at the yard, and I just get this overwhelming sense that there's no good version of the future coming. It's just a constant, low, sad feeling.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, or has that changed lately?

That has definitely changed. I used to always make time for things like hiking, or yoga... working in my garden, taking bird photos. But lately, I just keep canceling plans. My camera has just been sitting in the closet. It's just... none of it really feels worth the effort right now.
Do you still take pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, even if you're not motivated to do them?

No, not really. I mean... if I do force myself to go out to the garden or something, it just feels like going through the motions. I don't get any joy out of it once I'm out there. It just feels flat.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
No, my weight has been about the same. I haven't noticed any real change there.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, mostly on the slower side. My husband actually pointed it out to me recently. He says I move around the house like I'm underwater lately. And when he asks me something, even just a really simple question, it can take me a while to answer him because... I don't know, the words just come out so slowly right now.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Yes, I have. Um... mostly late at night. I'll just be lying there and I catch myself thinking that my husband might be better off without me. I haven't made a plan to do anything or hurt myself, but... the thought just keeps coming back. It happens enough that it actually scares me.
How often do you have these thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't been keeping track of the exact number of times. It's mostly just... when I'm lying awake in the dark, the thoughts sort of creep in. But I couldn't give you a specific number of days or anything like that.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... it's been about two months. It started right around the time we took on our new mortgage. Before that, I was in this sort of overcharged business push, but ever since the mortgage, my mood just swung right into this long, low stretch.
Have you been feeling restless or unable to sit still at any point?

Yeah, before this low period hit, I had this burst where I just... I couldn't sit still at all. I kept jumping up from my desk to sketch out new office layouts, or I'd start reorganizing all my files. I'd keep finding one more task to start, even when there was no real reason it had to happen right then. It was like I just had to keep moving.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt better, with improved mood and energy, since this low period started two months ago?
No, not at all. It's just been a steady low this whole time. I haven't had any days where I felt better or had my energy back since it started.
Did you experience a period of time before these two months where you felt unusually happy, energetic, or irritable for several days or longer?

Yes, I did. In those first few weeks right after we signed the mortgage papers, I felt... almost lit up. Like I was completely unstoppable one minute. But then, the next minute, I'd just snap at my husband or my coworkers over tiny delays. So yeah, it was a lot of energy, but I was also really irritable if things didn't move fast enough.
Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or energy levels during these two months?

No, I haven't. Like I mentioned a moment ago, it's just been a constant low. There hasn't been any break in it or any days where I felt my mood or energy pick back up. It's just been steady like this the whole two months.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt nearly normal, but then your symptoms worsened again?
No, honestly, it's just like I was saying... there haven't been any ups and downs like that. I haven't felt normal for even a day. It's just been a flat, steady low this entire time.
Would you describe your current low mood and associated symptoms as mild, moderate, or severe?

I would say it's moderate. It's not so severe that I can't get out of bed at all, but it's definitely bad enough that it's making my job as a market research analyst really difficult. It's just a constant struggle to get through the day.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in, even if you don't feel motivated to do them?

Not really, no. I used to make time for things like hiking, yoga, working in my garden, and taking bird photos. But lately, I just keep canceling my plans or letting my camera sit in the closet. It just... none of it feels worth the effort right now. So, no, I'm not really getting any enjoyment out of those things anymore.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt extremely happy, energetic, or irritable for several days or longer before these past two months?

Yes, I did. Um, it was during the first few weeks after we signed the mortgage papers for our house. I remember feeling almost... lit up, I guess you could say. Like I was completely unstoppable one minute. But then, the next minute, I'd just snap at my husband or get really short with my coworkers over tiny little delays. So yeah, I definitely had a period like that where my energy and mood were just all over the place.
Did your period of feeling lit up and unstoppable, with increased irritability, last for at least four consecutive days?
Yes, it definitely lasted at least four days. It was a solid two weeks of feeling exactly like that before things leveled out again.
Did your period of feeling lit up and unstoppable, with increased irritability, occur before your current two-month period of low mood?

Yes, it did. Um, since we took on the mortgage about two months ago, my mood swung from that overcharged, unstoppable feeling right into this... this low stretch I'm in now. So the high energy definitely came first.
Has your current low mood lasted for at least two weeks?
Yes, definitely longer than two weeks. Um, that depressed, just slowed-down and exhausted feeling... it's been going on most days for about the past two months now.
